seen_animation: A paintbrush drawn in black line: a closed pointed bristle shape filled with zigzag scribble at the top, and two lines for the handle running down and off the bottom edge. Grey scenery is a wavy mark at top-left, a curved line at lower-left, and a vertical line near the right edge. In frame 1 the bristle tip is at upper centre with a short grey line beside it. In frame 2 the brush is shifted right and slightly up. In frames 3-5 it sits back near the frame 1 position while a grey line grows up and to the right from the tip. In frames 6-15 the brush moves down and to the left in steps, and the grey line behind it lengthens, so the brush is drawing a long diagonal stroke from upper right toward lower left. In frame 16 the brush has been lifted back up and to the right, to the upper part of the stroke.
seen_film: A close-up of a real paintbrush with dark bristles and a clear plastic ferrule, tip pointing up, held over a tan surface with a dark curl at top-left and a curved dark mark at lower-left. Frame 1 has the tip at upper centre; frame 2 the brush jumps right; frames 3-5 it returns to the upper-centre area and a faint diagonal line appears up-right of the tip. Frames 6-15 the brush travels down and left, leaving a lengthening faint diagonal stroke; frames 11, 12 and 15 show motion blur from fast movement. Frame 16 the brush has moved back up and right and is blurred.
named_subject: a paintbrush (bristle tip with hatched scribble, handle below)
evidence: Tip positions match the film within a few pixels in every frame: frame 1 (about 148,125 vs 145,125), frame 2 shifted right (about 168,110 vs 160,105 in-cell), frame 6 dropped down-left (about 118,148 in-cell in both), frame 8 (about 105,160 in both), frame 11 (about 92,165 in both), frame 13 (about 100,160 in both), frame 15 lowest-left point (about 72,185 vs 75,180), frame 16 jump back up-right (about 170,130 vs 170,120). The grey diagonal stroke line lengthens from short in frames 1-5 to long in frames 6-16, as the faint painted line does in the film. The jumps at frames 2, 6 and 16 are present in the film too. The bristle outline with zigzag hatching in every frame is the same construction as the bristles in c.png.
primary_gap: The handle is drawn as two open lines that run off the frame, whereas the doodle's handle is a closed outline with a narrow neck at the bristles, so the brush body is less recognisably the doodle's than the bristle tip is.
closes_when: Where the handle is visible, its two lines join the bristle at a narrow neck that matches c.png's neck width and keep that same pair of lines with the same spacing and taper in every frame.
protect: The per-frame placement of the bristle tip that tracks the film exactly; the growing grey stroke line; the jumps only at frames 2, 6 and 16 where the film has them; the doodle's closed pointed bristle outline with zigzag hatching; the tip-up orientation that follows the film.
identity_gap: The bristle tip is the doodle's drawing, but the handle is simplified to two open lines and the bristle hatching is redrawn slightly differently from frame to frame.
